intent.raw_query: Patagonia hiking Torres del Paine, $4500, 12 days, December 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route that winds through the most spectacular landscapes of Torres del Paine, including the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the base of the iconic Torres towers. Camp or stay in mountain refugios along the route and witness breathtaking Patagonian scenery at every turn.
experiences.location: Central Torres del Paine National Park, Patagonia

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike approximately 4-5 hours to the iconic viewpoint at the base of the three granite towers. Witness the legendary alpenglow as the first light of sunrise paints the towers in shades of gold and pink, reflecting in the turquoise glacial lake below. One of the most photographed moments in all of Patagonia.
experiences.location: Sector Las Torres, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through the icy waters of Lago Grey surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided kayaking tour brings you up close to the stunning blue ice walls of the glacier, offering a unique water-level perspective of this natural wonder that few trekkers experience.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Western Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and towering granite walls. Hike to the Mirador Británico viewpoint for a panoramic 360-degree view of the Paine Massif, Glacier Francés, and surrounding peaks. Wildlife sightings of condors and guanacos are common along this trail.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari
experiences.description: Join an expert naturalist guide for a dawn or dusk wildlife tracking excursion in the park's open pampas and valleys. Torres del Paine has one of the highest densities of wild pumas in the world, and this guided experience dramatically increases your chances of spotting these elusive big cats alongside guanacos, Andean foxes, rheas, and condors in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga and Pampas Sector, Eastern Torres del Paine National Park

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Torres del Paine, Patagonia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to accommodation near Torres del Paine. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, unpack, and rest. Review trail maps and plan the week ahead.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick sandwich or empanadas from a 24-hour kiosk near the airport or bus terminal — budget ~$5-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your shuttle from Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales to save money. Shared shuttles cost around $10-20 USD vs $80+ for private taxis. Download offline maps (Maps.me or Gaia GPS) before landing. Exchange some cash as many budget spots in Patagonia prefer pesos.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a slow morning at the resort. Organize your trekking gear, pack essentials, and pick up your Torres del Paine National Park entrance permit if not already purchased online (budget ~$35 USD). Study trail maps over coffee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short orientation walk around the resort area and nearby lakeshore to acclimate to the Patagonian wind and altitude. Explore the immediate surroundings, spot local birdlife including condors and upland geese. Visit the nearest ranger station to confirm trail conditions and current weather forecasts.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Puerto Natales (if nearby) or the closest village for a casual dinner. Visit the local market to stock up on budget trail snacks: nuts, dried fruit, crackers, instant noodles, and energy bars for the coming days of trekking.

meals.breakfast: Self-prepared at accommodation — instant oatmeal, coffee, fruit. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Light picnic near the lakeshore with bread, cheese, and cold cuts purchased at a local grocery. Budget ~$5 USD
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant in Puerto Natales — try a hearty cazuela (Chilean stew) or a set lunch menu (menú del día). Budget ~$8-12 USD

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally light to allow recovery from travel. Patagonian weather is highly unpredictable — use this day to check forecasts on weather.com or Windy.com and mentally prepare for wind, rain, and sun all in the same day. Hydrate well.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — rise at 04:00 and depart by 04:30 to reach the trailhead. The hike is approximately 4-5 hours to the iconic viewpoint at the base of the three granite towers. Bring headlamps, warm layers, and a packed breakfast to eat at the top as the sunrise paints the towers golden.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the trail back toward the trailhead (approximately 3-4 hours down). Take your time on the descent to enjoy the forest, suspension bridges, and river views. Arrive back at the base camp area by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by shuttle or on foot. Hot shower, rest sore muscles, and do light stretching. Prepare and eat a warm home-cooked meal at the resort using groceries purchased the day before.

meals.breakfast: Packed breakfast eaten at the Mirador — energy bars, nuts, instant coffee in a thermos. Budget ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Packed sandwich and fruit eaten on the trail descent. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta with canned tomato sauce and vegetables at accommodation. Budget ~$4 USD

day_by_day.notes: This is the crown jewel hike of Torres del Paine. The round trip is approximately 18-22 km with 800m elevation gain. Wear waterproof boots and bring trekking poles. The final boulder field scramble to the mirador is steep — take your time. Start early to beat crowds and catch the best light.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest day — gentle morning walk along the shores of Lago del Toro or nearby lagoon. Practice wildlife spotting: look for guanacos, rheas (ñandú), Andean condors, and flamingos in the shallower lake areas. Bring binoculars if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Salto Grande waterfall, a powerful cascade connecting Lago Nordenskjöld and Lago Pehoé. The short 20-minute walk from the parking area is free and spectacular. Explore the surrounding viewpoints and photograph the turquoise glacial waters.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from a lakeside vantage point near the resort. The long Patagonian summer evenings mean golden hour can last until 21:30-22:00. Journal your experiences, review photos, and plan the Valle del Francés hike.

meals.breakfast: Bread, jam, eggs, and instant coffee at accommodation. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Picnic at Salto Grande viewpoint — crackers, tuna, cheese, and fruit. Budget ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Budget parrilla (grill) meal — shared lamb or chicken dish at a local estancia or simple restaurant. Budget ~$10-14 USD

day_by_day.notes: Active rest days are essential in multi-day trekking trips to prevent injury. Use this day to air out boots, dry any wet gear, and treat any blisters. Salto Grande is accessible by park shuttle buses — check the CONAF schedule for budget-friendly transport options.

day_by_day.morning: Valle del Francés Day Hike — depart early by 07:00. Take the park catamaran or shuttle to the Paine Grande area (budget catamaran ~$20-25 USD round trip). Begin the trek into Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers and dramatic granite walls. The trail ascends through lenga beech forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mirador Británico (the highest viewpoint in the valley) for panoramic views of glaciers, waterfalls, and the Cuernos del Paine peaks. Listen for the thunderous crack of calving glaciers. Eat lunch at the mirador and soak in the wilderness before descending.
day_by_day.evening: Return via the same trail and catch the afternoon catamaran back. Arrive at base by early evening. Prepare a hearty meal to refuel after the long day. Estimated total distance: 22-26 km round trip.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with honey and banana at accommodation before departure. Budget ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Mirador Británico — peanut butter wraps, nuts, chocolate, and hot tea from thermos. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked rice, lentils, and canned vegetables at accommodation. Budget ~$4 USD

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is part of the famous W Trek. The hike to Mirador Británico adds significant elevation gain — only attempt if legs have recovered from Day 3. Weather in the valley changes rapidly; pack rain gear even on clear mornings. The catamaran schedule is seasonal — confirm times the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning. Sleep until 08:00. Light yoga or stretching session outdoors. Spend time organizing photos, writing travel notes, and doing laundry. Check weather forecast for the coming days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to Mirador Condor, a shorter and less-visited viewpoint accessible from the resort area. The 2-3 hour round trip offers excellent views of the surrounding pampa and lake system. High chance of spotting Andean condors riding thermal currents above the cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the resort area at sunset. If budget allows, treat yourself to one slightly nicer dinner at a local restaurant to celebrate the halfway point of the trip. Alternatively, prepare a special self-cooked meal with a bottle of inexpensive Chilean Carménère wine (~$5 USD at grocery stores).

meals.breakfast: Pancakes or scrambled eggs cooked at accommodation. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Soup and bread at accommodation or a simple café. Budget ~$5 USD
meals.dinner: Splurge meal — grilled salmon or lamb at a mid-range local restaurant, or self-cooked steak with wine. Budget ~$15-18 USD

day_by_day.notes: Halfway point of the trip — a great time to reassess your body's condition, gear, and remaining budget. Stock up on any supplies running low. Chilean wine is excellent quality and very affordable — a great way to celebrate on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Early hike to Lago Grey viewpoint. Depart by 07:30 and trek to the shores of Lago Grey to witness the stunning blue icebergs calved from Glaciar Grey floating in the turquoise water. The trail through lenga beech forest is relatively flat and accessible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend time at the Lago Grey shoreline photographing icebergs and watching for wildlife. Optional: short kayak rental near the glacier area if budget permits (~$20-30 USD for 1-2 hours). Return to resort by early afternoon via trail.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the nearest lakeshore. Cook a simple dinner and spend the evening star-gazing — Patagonia's dark skies offer incredible views of the Milky Way and Magellanic Clouds on clear nights.

meals.breakfast: Granola, yogurt, and coffee at accommodation. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — crackers, hummus, dried mango, and nuts. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked vegetable curry with rice at accommodation. Budget ~$4 USD

day_by_day.notes: Lago Grey is one of the most photogenic spots in the park. Bring extra memory cards or clear space on your phone. The trail to Lago Grey is part of the W Trek's western arm. Icebergs are most numerous after periods of warm weather when the glacier calves more frequently.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Laguna Azul and the northeastern sector of the park. This less-visited area offers solitude and excellent wildlife viewing — guanacos are extremely abundant here. The drive or shuttle to Laguna Azul takes about 1.5 hours from the main park area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the trail around Laguna Azul (approximately 3-4 hours, relatively flat). The lagoon reflects the Paine Massif on calm days creating mirror-like reflections. Watch for pumas in this sector — it's one of the best areas in the park for puma sightings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort by evening shuttle. Prepare dinner and spend the evening reviewing wildlife photos. Research and book any remaining activities or transport for the final days.

meals.breakfast: Toast, eggs, and coffee at accommodation. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Laguna Azul — sandwiches, fruit, and hot tea. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.dinner: Shared pot of homemade vegetable soup and bread at accommodation. Budget ~$4 USD

day_by_day.notes: The northeastern sector is often skipped by tourists doing the W Trek, making it a hidden gem for wildlife and solitude. Puma sightings are never guaranteed but this area has a higher density. Move quietly and scan the hillsides carefully. Bring your longest camera lens if you have one.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Cuernos hike — a moderate 3-4 hour round trip hike to a viewpoint overlooking the dramatic Cuernos del Paine (Horns of Paine), the jagged dark-capped peaks that are the park's most iconic silhouette. Best photographed in morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the hike and spend the afternoon relaxing at the resort. Optional: rent a bicycle from a local outfitter (~$10-15 USD/half day) to explore the flat roads around the resort area and nearby viewpoints without hiking.
day_by_day.evening: Prepare a celebratory camp-style dinner — grilled sausages, roasted vegetables, and potatoes cooked over a camp stove or resort BBQ area. Share stories with other budget travelers at the accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Muesli and milk with coffee at accommodation. Budget ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.dinner: BBQ-style sausages and vegetables with Chilean bread (marraqueta). Budget ~$6 USD

day_by_day.notes: The Cuernos del Paine are most dramatic in early morning and late evening light. If cycling, stay on designated roads and be aware of strong crosswinds which can make cycling challenging. Lock bikes when not in use. Check with resort about BBQ facilities in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Christmas Eve morning. Sleep in, enjoy a special breakfast, and take a slow walk around the resort grounds. Spend time reflecting on the trip and writing postcards or messages home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the park's administration center and CONAF ranger station for a free educational exhibit about the park's ecology, geology, and conservation history. Explore the nearby botanical garden area showcasing native Patagonian flora.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve dinner — splurge slightly on a festive meal. Many local restaurants and estancias offer special Christmas Eve dinners. Alternatively, prepare a special self-cooked feast at the accommodation with Chilean wine, roasted chicken, and traditional Chilean pan de Pascua (Christmas fruit cake) from a local bakery.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas Eve breakfast — fresh fruit, scrambled eggs, toast, and good coffee. Budget ~$5 USD
meals.lunch: Light lunch at accommodation. Budget ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Festive Christmas Eve dinner — roasted chicken, potatoes, salad, and wine. Self-cooked or budget restaurant. Budget ~$15-20 USD

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is celebrated enthusiastically in Chile. Expect some local festivities and a warm atmosphere. Many shops may close early on December 24th, so stock up on groceries in the morning. The long summer daylight means it stays light until nearly 22:30, making for a magical evening.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning sunrise hike to a nearby viewpoint to watch the sun rise over the Andes — a magical and unforgettable Christmas gift to yourself. Bring hot chocolate or coffee in a thermos and enjoy the solitude of early morning in Patagonia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final major hike of the trip — revisit your favorite trail or explore a shorter route you haven't done yet. Consider the Lago Sarmiento circuit or the trail to Mirador Ferrier for a final Patagonian adventure. Take your time and savor every moment.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Torres del Paine. Begin packing non-essential gear. Take a long sunset walk and photograph the landscape one last time. Enjoy a relaxed dinner and toast to an incredible journey through one of the world's most spectacular wilderness areas.

meals.breakfast: Hot chocolate and Christmas cookies or pan de Pascua on the sunrise hike. Budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed Christmas picnic on the trail — special treats, chocolate, and remaining snacks. Budget ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Final dinner in the park — splurge on a proper restaurant meal or cook a memorable last supper at accommodation with remaining groceries. Budget ~$12-15 USD

day_by_day.notes: Feliz Navidad! Christmas Day in Patagonia is a truly unique experience. Many facilities may have reduced hours. Plan the day to be self-sufficient. Take time to thank any resort staff who made your stay special — tipping is appreciated in Chilean hospitality culture.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise over the Patagonian landscape. Complete packing and check out of the resort. Take final photos of the accommodation and surroundings. Settle any outstanding bills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrange shared shuttle or bus transfer back to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas depending on your onward travel plans. The journey takes approximately 2-3 hours. Upon arrival in Puerto Natales, explore the town briefly — visit the Milodon Cave museum area or browse artisan shops for budget-friendly souvenirs like locally made wool items.
day_by_day.evening: If departing from Punta Arenas, continue the transfer. Enjoy a farewell dinner in Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas at a local restaurant. Reflect on 12 extraordinary days in one of the world's most breathtaking national parks.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at accommodation before checkout — use remaining food supplies. Budget ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Lunch in Puerto Natales — try a traditional Chilean completo (hot dog) or empanadas from a local bakery. Budget ~$5 USD
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a budget restaurant in Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas — centolla (king crab) soup or a classic cazuela. Budget ~$10-14 USD

day_by_day.notes: Book your return shuttle in advance — spots fill up quickly in peak summer season (December-February). Keep your park entrance receipt as a souvenir. Declare any fresh food items at customs if crossing international borders. Budget summary: Aim for $50-70 USD/day including park entrance, food, transport, and activities for a true budget Patagonia experience.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight UA arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30. Collect luggage, meet pre-arranged transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in Torres del Paine. Check in, settle into your Beachfront room, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.lunch: On the plane or at departure airport
meals.dinner: Grab a light snack from the airport kiosk or a convenience stop en route — arrival is late so keep it simple. Alternatively, request a late arrival meal pack from the resort in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your airport transfer before departure. The drive from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine National Park takes approximately 1.5–2 hours. Confirm check-in time with Aegean Bliss Resort for late arrivals. Pack a small carry-on snack bag for the journey. December is peak Patagonian summer — daylight lasts until nearly 11 PM, so the landscape will still be visible on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning getting oriented — walk the resort grounds, take in the beachfront views of the lake, and pick up any gear or supplies you may need from the resort shop or nearby outfitter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation hike: Take the short, easy trail near the resort along the lakeshore to get your legs moving and acclimate to the Patagonian landscape. Enjoy views of the Paine Massif from the waterfront. Spend time reviewing maps and planning your W Trek logistics with resort staff or a local guide service.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the resort. Attend an optional park orientation briefing if offered by the resort. Enjoy sunset over the lake from your beachfront room — December sunsets can occur after 10 PM.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — fuel up with eggs, local bread, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café or pack a simple sandwich from the resort kitchen to enjoy on the lakeshore walk
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's main restaurant — try a classic Patagonian lamb dish (cordero al palo) or grilled trout. Budget approximately $25–40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a true rest and acclimatization day. Patagonian weather can be intense — use the afternoon to check forecasts for the coming days and adjust the itinerary accordingly. Purchase or rent any missing trekking gear (trekking poles, gaiters, wind layers) today. Confirm W Trek permits and refugio bookings if not already done — these must be booked well in advance during peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari (Dawn Excursion): Rise early and join an expert naturalist guide for a dawn wildlife tracking excursion in the park's open pampas and valley areas. Depart around 5:30–6:00 AM to maximize chances of spotting pumas, guanacos, condors, and foxes in the golden morning light. Duration approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort by midday. Rest, shower, and have lunch. Spend the afternoon doing a self-guided walk to Mirador Lago Toro or another easy viewpoint near the resort. Review and pack gear for the upcoming W Trek multi-day section beginning tomorrow.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner at the resort and pack your trekking bags for the W Trek. Lay out all gear, prepare snacks and trail food, and get to bed early for an early start tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early pre-safari light breakfast provided by guide service or grab a banana and coffee at the resort before departure; full breakfast on return
meals.lunch: Resort café lunch — hearty soup, sandwich, and juice to recover from the early morning
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant — pasta or rice-based dish for carb-loading before the trek. Budget $25–35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The wildlife safari is best at dawn or dusk. Book this experience in advance through the resort or a local operator such as Fantastico Sur or Fortaleza Expeditions. Dress in neutral, layered colors. Bring binoculars. This is one of the best opportunities in the world to see wild pumas — patience and silence are key. Confirm W Trek refugio bookings for Days 4–8 tonight.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 1: Transfer to the Laguna Amarga entrance or Pudeto catamaran dock. Begin the W Trek from the east, taking the catamaran across Lago Pehoé to Refugio Paine Grande. Arrive and check in to your refugio or campsite. Drop non-essential gear and begin the afternoon leg.
day_by_day.afternoon: W Trek — Valle del Francés Day Hike (first leg): From Refugio Paine Grande, hike northeast into the Valle del Francés — a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, dramatic granite walls, and the sound of avalanches echoing off Cerro Paine Grande. Hike to Mirador Británico (approximately 4–5 hours round trip, 16 km). Marvel at the amphitheater of peaks surrounding you.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Paine Grande by early evening. Enjoy a hot communal dinner at the refugio dining hall. Share stories with fellow trekkers. Rest and prepare for tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before transfer — eggs, toast, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch prepared by the resort or purchased at Refugio Paine Grande — energy bars, cheese, crackers, dried fruit, nuts
meals.dinner: Hot dinner at Refugio Paine Grande — typically a set menu of soup, main course (pasta or stew), and dessert. Budget approximately $25–30 USD per person included or added to refugio package.

day_by_day.notes: The catamaran from Pudeto to Refugio Paine Grande runs at set times (typically 9:00 AM and 12:00 PM in peak season) — confirm schedule in advance and book tickets. The Valle del Francés hike is one of the most spectacular in Patagonia. Weather can change rapidly — carry full rain gear, extra layers, and sunscreen. Trekking poles are highly recommended for the steep sections.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 2: After breakfast at the refugio, hike west from Refugio Paine Grande toward the Grey Glacier sector. The trail follows the southern shore of Lago Grey with stunning views of the turquoise lake and floating icebergs. Approximately 4–5 hours to Refugio Grey (11 km). Check in and drop your pack.
day_by_day.afternoon: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition: In the afternoon, join a guided kayaking excursion on Lago Grey, paddling through icy waters surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. Get up-close views of the glacier's towering blue ice face. Duration approximately 2.5–3 hours. This is an unforgettable and unique Patagonian experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Refugio Grey. Hot shower (if available), warm up by the communal fire or heater, and enjoy dinner at the refugio. Rest well — tomorrow is a long day.

meals.breakfast: Refugio Paine Grande breakfast — oatmeal, bread, jam, coffee, juice
meals.lunch: Trail lunch eaten on the hike to Refugio Grey — packed snacks, energy bars, sandwiches
meals.dinner: Hot set dinner at Refugio Grey — hearty stew, bread, and dessert. Budget included in refugio package or approximately $25 USD.

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier kayaking must be pre-booked through a licensed operator (Big Foot Patagonia is a well-regarded local provider). Dry bags are provided but bring a change of dry clothes for after. The afternoon light on the glacier is spectacular. Lago Grey can be extremely windy — the excursion may be weather-dependent. Have a backup plan to simply hike to the glacier viewpoint on foot if kayaking is cancelled.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek — Day 3: Hike back from Refugio Grey to Refugio Paine Grande (reverse the Day 2 trail, approximately 4–5 hours). Enjoy the same stunning Lago Grey scenery from a different direction — often the light and perspective make it feel entirely new. Arrive at Refugio Paine Grande for lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east from Refugio Paine Grande along the southern arm of the W toward Refugio Los Cuernos (approximately 3–4 hours, 11 km). The trail passes through lenga beech forest and open pampas with jaw-dropping views of Los Cuernos (The Horns) — the jagged, two-toned granite and sedimentary peaks that are among Patagonia's most iconic sights.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy dinner. The location here offers extraordinary sunset views of Los Cuernos reflected in Lago Nordenskjöld.

meals.breakfast: Refugio Grey breakfast — bread, eggs, coffee, fruit
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten at Refugio Paine Grande or on the trail — resupply any snacks at the refugio shop
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Los Cuernos — set menu, typically includes soup and a warm main. Budget $25–30 USD.

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest day of the W Trek in terms of total distance covered (combining the return from Grey and the leg to Los Cuernos). Pace yourself and start early. The trail between Paine Grande and Los Cuernos is well-marked but has some exposed, windy sections above the lake. Carry at least 2 liters of water. Trekking poles are helpful on the rocky sections.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — Preparation Day: Rise early at Refugio Los Cuernos and hike the final eastern leg of the W Trek to Refugio Las Torres (approximately 3–4 hours, 11 km along the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld). Arrive at the Las Torres sector by midday. Check in to Refugio Las Torres or Chileno.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rest, hydrate, and prepare for the pre-dawn summit hike tomorrow. Do a short acclimatization walk up the lower section of the Las Torres trail to scout the route. Enjoy the views of the valley. Visit the small shop at the refugio for any last-minute snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Early dinner at the refugio — a hearty, high-calorie meal to fuel tomorrow's big hike. Set alarms for 4:00–4:30 AM. Get to sleep by 8:00–9:00 PM.

meals.breakfast: Refugio Los Cuernos breakfast — oatmeal, bread, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the hike to Las Torres sector
meals.dinner: Hot dinner at Refugio Las Torres or Chileno — pasta, meat, soup. Budget $25–30 USD.

day_by_day.notes: The Mirador Las Torres sunrise hike is the crown jewel of the W Trek and requires an extremely early start — ideally departing the refugio by 4:30–5:00 AM to reach the mirador at sunrise (which in December occurs around 5:30–6:00 AM). Confirm sunrise time the night before. The hike to the mirador is approximately 4–5 hours round trip from Refugio Chileno, with a steep, boulder-scramble final section. Headlamps are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike: Wake at 4:00 AM. Depart Refugio Chileno by 4:30 AM with headlamps. Hike approximately 2–2.5 hours through lenga beech forest and up a steep moraine to reach the glacial lake at the base of the three granite towers — Torres del Paine. Arrive just before sunrise and witness the towers turn from grey to gold to blazing orange as the first light strikes them. This is one of the most iconic and emotional moments in South American trekking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from the mirador (approximately 2 hours back to the refugio). Enjoy a well-deserved late breakfast at the refugio. Transfer back to Aegean Bliss Resort by shuttle or pre-arranged vehicle (approximately 1–1.5 hours). Check back in, shower, and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Celebration dinner at the resort's restaurant — you've completed the W Trek. Treat yourself to a special meal with Patagonian lamb, local wine, and dessert.

meals.breakfast: Very light pre-hike snack (energy bar, banana) before departure; full hot breakfast at the refugio on return
meals.lunch: Light packed lunch on the trail or at the refugio before transfer
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — splurge slightly on a Patagonian lamb or seafood dish with a glass of Chilean Carménère. Budget $35–50 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Weather on the morning of Day 8 is critical — if clouds obscure the towers at sunrise, consider waiting up to an hour as they often clear. The boulder field at the top is slippery when wet — trekking poles and careful footing are essential. Carry a warm layer as the mirador is extremely cold and windy even in summer. The return to the resort is a triumphant and emotional moment — savor it.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day. Sleep in as long as needed. Enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning reading, journaling, or simply sitting on your beachfront balcony watching the lake and mountains. Optional: gentle yoga or stretching to ease sore muscles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely afternoon activity: Take a short, flat nature walk along the lakeshore near the resort, keeping eyes open for Andean condors, black-necked swans, and flamingos that frequent the Patagonian lakes. Alternatively, visit the resort spa if available for a massage to recover from the trek. Browse any local artisan stalls near the park entrance for souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks on the beachfront terrace — order a Pisco Sour and watch the alpenglow light up the Paine Massif. Dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet — take your time and eat well
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café — salad, soup, and fresh juice
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant dinner — try the local centolla (king crab) if available, or a hearty cazuela (Chilean stew). Budget $25–40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: This rest day is essential after the physical demands of the W Trek (approximately 70–80 km over 5 days). Do not plan any strenuous activity. Use this time to do laundry, recharge electronics, and reorganize gear. December 23rd is two days before Christmas — the resort may have special holiday decorations or events beginning. Ask the concierge about any upcoming seasonal activities.

day_by_day.morning: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari (Dusk/Dawn — Second Opportunity): For those who want another chance at wildlife, join a second wildlife tracking excursion at dawn. Alternatively, take a self-guided drive or guided vehicle tour through the park's open pampas areas — the Laguna Azul and Laguna Amarga areas are excellent for guanaco herds and condor sightings. Bring a telephoto lens if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Valle del Francés Scenic Viewpoint Drive: If legs are recovered, take a half-day guided excursion to a viewpoint overlooking the Valle del Francés from the road, enjoying the panoramic perspective of the hanging glaciers and granite walls without a full day's hike. Alternatively, relax at the resort and enjoy the beachfront setting.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Celebration Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort. Many Patagonian resorts host a special Nochebuena dinner with traditional Chilean and Patagonian dishes, live music, and a festive atmosphere. Enjoy the communal celebration with fellow guests.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before the wildlife excursion, or full buffet if taking a later start
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch enjoyed at a scenic park viewpoint, or resort café on return
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at the resort — expect a multi-course feast with Patagonian lamb, seafood, empanadas, and Chilean wine. Budget $45–60 USD per person for the special dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm with the resort in advance whether a special Christmas Eve dinner is offered and whether reservations are required. This is a magical evening in Patagonia — the long summer daylight means it will still be light at 10 PM. Toast the season with a glass of Chilean sparkling wine (espumante) as the sun sets behind the Paine Massif. A truly unforgettable Christmas Eve.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Morning Nature Walk: Begin Christmas Day with a peaceful sunrise walk along the lakeshore near the resort. The early morning light on the Paine Massif on a clear day is extraordinary. Bring binoculars for birdwatching — December is peak season for Andean condors, upland geese, and Magellanic woodpeckers in the park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Grey Glacier Boat Excursion (Alternative to Kayaking): Take a half-day boat tour on Lago Grey to view the Grey Glacier up close from the water — a more relaxed alternative to kayaking. The boat passes enormous floating icebergs and approaches the glacier face for dramatic photographs. Duration approximately 3 hours. Return to resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort. Enjoy a festive holiday dinner with fellow guests. Reflect on the incredible week of trekking and wildlife encounters. Exchange stories with new friends made on the trail.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas morning breakfast at the resort — expect a more elaborate spread with pastries, fresh fruit, smoked salmon, and champagne or sparkling juice
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat tour or at the resort on return — sandwiches, empanadas, hot chocolate
meals.dinner: Christmas Day dinner at the resort — a celebratory multi-course meal. Budget $40–55 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier boat tour is operated by Grey Glacier Navigation and departs from Refugio Grey or a designated dock — confirm departure point and book in advance. On Christmas Day, some services may operate on a holiday schedule — confirm all bookings the day before. This is a wonderful, unhurried day to soak in the magic of Patagonia at Christmas. Consider writing postcards or calling family from the resort to share the experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final Morning in Patagonia: Wake up early one last time to catch the morning light on the lake and mountains from your beachfront room. Take a final short walk along the shore, breathing in the crisp Patagonian air. Pack your bags and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Take photos of the resort and surroundings for lasting memories.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas airport for your onward flight. En route, stop at a viewpoint for a final look at the Torres del Paine massif — a proper farewell to one of the world's great wilderness destinations. Arrive at the airport with ample time for check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Patagonia. If your flight is in the evening or you have a long layover in Punta Arenas, visit the historic Plaza de Armas, browse the Mercado Municipal for local souvenirs (Patagonian wool products, local chocolates, artisan crafts), and enjoy a final Chilean meal at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — make it count with a full hot breakfast
meals.lunch: En route lunch stop in Puerto Natales — try Restaurante La Mesita Grande for excellent pizza and local beer, or Afrigonia for a creative fusion menu. Budget $15–25 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or Punta Arenas restaurant if time allows — La Cuisine or Santolla are good mid-range options in Punta Arenas for a final centolla king crab or Patagonian lamb meal. Budget $20–35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your transfer to the airport the night before and allow extra time — road conditions in Patagonia can be unpredictable. The drive from Torres del Paine to Punta Arenas airport takes approximately 4–5 hours; to Puerto Natales airport approximately 1.5 hours. Declare any food items at customs. Consider shipping any bulky souvenirs (wool blankets, etc.) from Puerto Natales post office to avoid baggage issues. Leave time to reflect on an extraordinary 12 days in one of the world's most spectacular wilderness destinations.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route that winds through the most spectacular landscapes of Torres del Paine, including the Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the base of the iconic Torres towers. Camp or stay in mountain refugios along the route and witness breathtaking Patagonian scenery at every turn.
experiences.location: Central Torres del Paine National Park, Patagonia

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Rise before dawn and hike approximately 4-5 hours to the iconic viewpoint at the base of the three granite towers. Witness the legendary alpenglow as the first light of sunrise paints the towers in shades of gold and pink, reflecting in the turquoise glacial lake below. One of the most photographed moments in all of Patagonia.
experiences.location: Sector Las Torres, Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through the icy waters of Lago Grey surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier. A guided kayaking tour brings you up close to the stunning blue ice walls of the glacier, offering a unique water-level perspective of this natural wonder that few trekkers experience.
experiences.location: Lago Grey, Western Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Hike
experiences.description: Trek through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and towering granite walls. Hike to the Mirador Británico viewpoint for a panoramic 360-degree view of the Paine Massif, Glacier Francés, and surrounding peaks. Wildlife sightings of condors and guanacos are common along this trail.
experiences.location: Valle del Francés, Central Torres del Paine National Park

experiences.name: Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari
experiences.description: Join an expert naturalist guide for a dawn or dusk wildlife tracking excursion in the park's open pampas and valleys. Torres del Paine has one of the highest densities of wild pumas in the world, and this guided experience dramatically increases your chances of spotting these elusive big cats alongside guanacos, Andean foxes, rheas, and condors in their natural habitat.
experiences.location: Laguna Amarga and Pampas Sector, Eastern Torres del Paine National Park

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort awaits at the terminal with a personal concierge. Scenic night drive to the resort with welcome champagne in the vehicle. Check-in to Beachfront suite with a personalized welcome amenity, hot herbal tea, and a light late-night snack prepared by the resort chef.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.lunch: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.dinner: Private late-night welcome platter in-suite: artisan Patagonian charcuterie, local cheeses, smoked lamb empanadas, and a bottle of Chilean Carménère — arranged by the resort ahead of arrival

day_by_day.notes: Flight arrives at 22:30. No day activities scheduled. Ensure resort is notified of late arrival in advance. Request early morning wake-up service and briefing kit for Day 2 activities to be left in suite upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely welcome breakfast at the resort's panoramic dining room overlooking the Patagonian landscape. Meet with your dedicated private guide for a full trip orientation and gear check. Take a relaxed orientation walk around the resort grounds and nearby lakeshore to acclimate to the altitude and environment — approximately 1-2 hours of gentle walking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided orientation excursion to Mirador Lago Sarmiento — a short scenic hike with sweeping views of the turquoise lake and the Torres del Paine massif in the background. This gentle 2-3 hour introduction hike allows your body to acclimatize. Return to resort for a full spa treatment — choose from a hot stone massage or Patagonian botanical body wrap at the resort spa.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails on the resort's private terrace with unobstructed views of the granite towers catching alpenglow. Private welcome dinner hosted by the resort's executive chef featuring a curated tasting menu of regional Patagonian cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort dining room — fresh-baked medialunas, Patagonian berry compote, smoked salmon, farm eggs cooked to order, and freshly pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light resort poolside lunch — grilled Patagonian lamb chops with quinoa salad, local king crab ceviche, and sparkling water with citrus
meals.dinner: Private chef's tasting menu at the resort restaurant: 6-course meal featuring Patagonian king crab, slow-roasted guanaco, wild mushroom risotto, and a curated Chilean wine pairing from the Maipo and Colchagua valleys

day_by_day.notes: Day 2 is intentionally relaxed to recover from overnight travel and acclimatize. Gear check with guide is essential — confirm trekking boots, layering system, waterproof jacket, and trekking poles are ready for Day 3 onwards.

day_by_day.morning: Early rise for the Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. Depart resort at 04:00 with private guide and headlamps. Trek approximately 4-5 hours through lenga beech forest and rocky moraine to reach the iconic viewpoint at the base of the three granite towers. Arrive at sunrise to witness the legendary alpenglow on the towers reflected in the glacial tarn below — one of the most photographed moments in Patagonia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend at a comfortable pace, stopping at scenic viewpoints along the trail. Return to resort by early afternoon. Enjoy a restorative resort spa session — deep tissue massage targeting legs and back. Optional: soak in the resort's outdoor heated pool with mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the resort. Private sommelier-led wine tasting session in the resort's cellar — exploring premium Chilean and Argentine Patagonian wines. Early dinner and rest in preparation for upcoming multi-day trek.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike packed gourmet breakfast prepared by resort chef: energy bars, fresh fruit, thermos of premium coffee, croissants with local jam, and hard-boiled eggs — consumed at trailhead or en route
meals.lunch: Trail lunch pack provided by resort: smoked trout sandwich on artisan bread, mixed nuts, dark chocolate, dried Patagonian berries, and electrolyte drinks
meals.dinner: À la carte dinner at resort restaurant — pan-seared Patagonian trout with herb butter and roasted root vegetables, followed by calafate berry tart with Patagonian cream

day_by_day.notes: 4:00 AM departure is essential to reach the mirador at sunrise. December offers long daylight hours — approximately 17+ hours of light. Weather in Torres del Paine is highly unpredictable; guide will assess conditions at 03:30 before departure. Full waterproof gear required.

day_by_day.morning: Begin the W Trek Multi-Day Hike — Day 1 of 4. Private luxury transfer to the Laguna Amarga ranger station entrance. Trek the eastern arm of the W toward Mirador Las Torres (alternative angle and approach from the Ascencio Valley). Enjoy the trail at a premium pace with your private guide, stopping for wildlife spotting — condors, guanacos, and Andean foxes are frequently seen along this route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking toward Refugio Las Torres area. Afternoon views of the Valle del Ascencio with hanging glaciers visible on the massif. Arrive at your premium private camp or luxury refugio accommodation — pre-arranged with full bedding, hot showers, and gourmet catering. Settle in and explore the immediate surroundings.
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks outside the refugio with panoramic tower views. Communal gourmet dinner at the luxury refugio dining tent — three-course meal prepared by an on-site chef. Stargazing session with your guide — December skies in Patagonia offer spectacular Milky Way visibility.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — eggs Benedict with smoked Patagonian salmon, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch pack: artisan sandwiches, energy snacks, fresh fruit, premium chocolate, and hot soup in a thermos
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at luxury refugio: roasted vegetable soup, slow-braised lamb shank with Patagonian herbs, and dulce de leche crepes for dessert — paired with Malbec

day_by_day.notes: This marks the start of the 4-day W Trek segment. Luggage transfer service arranged — only carry a daypack with essentials. Premium refugio or private camp accommodation pre-booked. Confirm dietary requirements with camp chef in advance.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 2 — Trek from Las Torres sector westward along the central spine of the W toward Valle del Francés. Morning trail passes through native lenga beech and ñirre forest with frequent condor sightings overhead. Cross the Río Francés bridge and begin the ascent into the valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Valle del Francés Day Hike integrated into the W Trek route. Trek through the glacially carved valley flanked by hanging glaciers and dramatic rock faces. Reach the upper mirador — Mirador Británico — for 360-degree views of the Cuernos del Paine, Glacier Francés, and the surrounding massif. Witness and listen to the thunderous calving of hanging glaciers. Descend and continue to luxury camp at Italiano or Cuernos sector.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at premium camp by late afternoon. Hot shower and change of clothes. Private guided evening session on Patagonian geology and glaciology by the campfire. Gourmet dinner under the stars with the Cuernos del Paine as a dramatic backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Hot camp breakfast: porridge with Patagonian honey and berries, scrambled eggs, toast, fresh juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten at Mirador Británico: gourmet wraps, energy balls, fruit, nuts, and hot tea from thermos
meals.dinner: Camp chef dinner: king crab bisque, grilled beef tenderloin with chimichurri and roasted potatoes, and warm calafate berry crumble with cream

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is considered one of the most dramatic sections of the W Trek. Weather can shift rapidly — hanging glacier calving is more frequent in the afternoon. Keep cameras ready throughout. Distance today is approximately 16-18 km with significant elevation gain.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — Trek from Cuernos/Italiano sector westward along the shores of Lago Nordenskjöld toward Paine Grande. Morning light on the Cuernos del Paine is exceptional — golden hour photography opportunity. Trail hugs the lakeshore with constant views of the turquoise glacial lake and the massif reflected in the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Paine Grande luxury camp/refugio. After settling in, join an optional short afternoon hike to Mirador Lago Grey for first views of the Grey Glacier — a dramatic ice field stretching to the horizon. Spot floating icebergs of brilliant blue in Lago Grey from the mirador.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Paine Grande for sunset cocktails on the deck overlooking Lago Grey. Evening briefing with guide on tomorrow's Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — safety protocols, equipment fitting, and route overview. Gourmet dinner and early rest.

meals.breakfast: Hot camp breakfast: French press coffee, granola with local yogurt and berries, avocado toast with poached eggs
meals.lunch: Lakeside picnic lunch on the shores of Lago Nordenskjöld: smoked meats, artisan cheeses, fresh bread, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Refugio Paine Grande premium dinner: Patagonian lamb stew with root vegetables, fresh bread, and a selection of Chilean red wines — dessert of fresh berry pavlova

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 of the W Trek is relatively flat and scenic — ideal for photography. Arrive at Paine Grande with enough time for the afternoon mirador walk. Confirm kayaking equipment sizing with guide this evening. Weather assessment for kayaking will be made at 06:00 tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — the highlight experience of the trip. Depart at 08:00 with expert certified guides. Don premium dry suits and safety gear. Paddle through the icy, brilliantly colored waters of Lago Grey surrounded by floating icebergs calved from the massive Grey Glacier — one of the largest glaciers in the Southern Patagonian Ice Field. Navigate between towering blue icebergs and approach the glacier face.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue kayaking along the glacier face, listening to the creak and groan of the living ice. Land on a rocky shore for a glacier walk with crampons — walk directly on the ancient ice and marvel at the blue crevasses and ice formations. Enjoy a champagne toast on the glacier — a truly once-in-a-lifetime moment. Return paddle to the launch point.
day_by_day.evening: W Trek Day 4 — final leg. Transfer or short trek back toward the park exit. Private luxury vehicle transfer returns guests to Aegean Bliss Resort. Long hot shower, resort spa recovery treatment, and a celebratory dinner marking the completion of the W Trek.

meals.breakfast: Pre-kayak hot breakfast at Paine Grande: oatmeal, eggs, toast, fruit, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on the glacier shoreline: smoked salmon on rye, artisan cheeses, premium chocolate, hot soup, and sparkling wine for the glacier toast
meals.dinner: Celebratory W Trek completion dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — chef's special tasting menu: 7-course Patagonian feast with wine pairing, ending with a personalized dessert celebrating the achievement

day_by_day.notes: Kayaking is weather-dependent — guide will confirm at 06:00. If conditions are unsuitable, an alternative Grey Glacier catamaran excursion will be substituted. Dry suits are provided but bring a thermal base layer. Waterproof camera or GoPro strongly recommended. This is the longest and most physically demanding day of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery day at Aegean Bliss Resort. Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely late breakfast. Morning resort spa session — choose from a full-body Patagonian mineral scrub, hot stone massage, or hydrotherapy circuit. Optional gentle yoga session on the resort's outdoor deck with mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari — depart at 14:00 with an expert naturalist guide for a dusk wildlife excursion in the park's open pampas and scrubland. Track pumas, guanacos, rheas, Andean condors, and Patagonian foxes. The guide uses radio-tracking data and expert field knowledge to maximize sighting opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort at sunset. Cocktail hour at the resort bar. Private stargazing experience arranged on the resort terrace — telescope set up by the resort's astronomy guide for views of the Southern Cross, Magellanic Clouds, and Milky Way core. Late dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent late breakfast in-suite — eggs Benedict, smoked salmon, pastry basket, fresh tropical fruits, mimosas, and specialty single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Resort poolside lunch: grilled Patagonian shrimp skewers, fresh ceviche, avocado salad, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Late dinner at resort restaurant: whole roasted Patagonian lamb carré with rosemary jus, truffle mashed potatoes, and a premium Cabernet Sauvignon from Maipo Valley

day_by_day.notes: Puma sightings are most likely at dawn or dusk — the afternoon safari timing is optimized for this. December is peak puma activity season as females are often accompanied by cubs. Bring binoculars and a long-lens camera. Dress in neutral earth tones to avoid startling wildlife.

day_by_day.morning: Dawn Puma and Wildlife Tracking Safari — second excursion, this time at first light (depart 05:00). Dawn offers the highest probability of puma sightings as they return from nocturnal hunts. Expert naturalist guide leads the excursion across the park's open grasslands and rocky outcrops. Photograph guanacos, condors soaring on thermals, and the dramatic morning light on the Paine massif.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort by mid-morning. Private fly-fishing experience on one of the region's pristine rivers — guided by a professional fly-fishing instructor, targeting Patagonian brown and rainbow trout. No experience necessary — full instruction provided. Enjoy the solitude of remote Patagonian river fishing with snow-capped peaks as a backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Resort chef prepares your catch — if successful, enjoy your personally caught trout pan-seared with capers and brown butter as part of your evening meal. Relax in the resort's private outdoor hot tub overlooking the lake and mountains at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn packed breakfast: thermos of coffee, energy bars, fruit, and croissants consumed during the safari
meals.lunch: Riverside picnic lunch during fly-fishing: gourmet sandwiches, local cheeses, fruit, and chilled sparkling water
meals.dinner: Personalized dinner at resort featuring your caught trout (if successful) alongside Patagonian king crab salad, seasonal vegetables, and a chilled Sauvignon Blanc from Casablanca Valley

day_by_day.notes: 5:00 AM departure for dawn safari — request a wake-up call at 04:15. Fly-fishing licenses are arranged by the resort. Catch-and-release policy applies unless guests wish to keep one fish for dinner. Waders and all fishing equipment provided.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve — Special Day. Private guided photography hike to Laguna Azul on the eastern side of the park — a less-visited, pristine turquoise lake with reflections of the Torres del Paine massif. The remote location offers solitude and exceptional wildlife encounters away from main tourist routes. Approximately 3-4 hours of moderate hiking.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for an afternoon of leisure. Optional: private horseback riding excursion through the Patagonian steppe with a local gaucho guide — experience the region as traditional ranchers have for centuries, riding through open grasslands with panoramic mountain views.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort. The resort hosts a special celebration with a curated multi-course feast, live Patagonian folk music, and a bonfire on the beach. Dress code: smart casual. Toast the season with premium Chilean sparkling wine under the Patagonian stars.

meals.breakfast: Christmas Eve special breakfast at resort: smoked salmon eggs royale, fresh pastries, fruit platter, and a glass of morning Cava
meals.lunch: Light pre-dinner lunch: Patagonian lamb empanadas, fresh salad, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala Dinner — 8-course tasting menu: king crab cocktail, pumpkin velouté, smoked trout tartare, palate cleanser sorbet, slow-roasted Patagonian lamb, cheese course with local honeys, and a bûche de Noël for dessert — premium wine pairing throughout

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve dinner is a signature resort event — confirm reservation and any dietary requirements at least 48 hours in advance. Smart casual attire recommended. The bonfire and live music typically run until midnight. A special Christmas gift amenity will be placed in-suite by the resort team.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — Leisurely start. Sleep in and enjoy a luxurious Christmas morning in-suite with a special holiday breakfast delivered by room service. Open any gifts or personal items brought for the occasion. Optional: a peaceful solo walk along the resort's private lakeshore trail to enjoy the morning light on the mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter scenic flight over Torres del Paine National Park — the ultimate Christmas gift experience. Fly over the Grey Glacier, the three Torres, the Cuernos del Paine, and the Southern Patagonian Ice Field for a bird's-eye perspective of the landscape you've been exploring on foot. Approximately 1.5-2 hours. Land at a remote viewpoint for a champagne picnic before returning.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas evening at the resort. Private in-suite couple's spa experience or solo indulgence — champagne, aromatherapy candles, and a personalized treatment. Christmas dinner at the resort with a special festive menu and live piano music.

meals.breakfast: Christmas in-suite breakfast: eggs any style, smoked salmon, fresh-baked pastries, fruit, orange juice, and a bottle of Moët & Chandon Champagne
meals.lunch: Helicopter champagne picnic at remote viewpoint: artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, charcuterie, fresh berries, and premium Champagne
meals.dinner: Christmas Day special dinner at resort: whole roasted Patagonian suckling pig with seasonal sides, traditional Chilean Christmas dishes, and a premium dessert spread — paired with Grand Cru Burgundy

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter flight is subject to weather conditions — a backup plan of a private catamaran cruise on Lago Grey will be arranged if flying is not possible.
